title: fix(cli): preserve sandbox ID after SSH setup failure
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16343

- Prints the created sandbox ID when local SSH setup fails, while retaining exit code 1 and the underlying error.
- Reports the partial setup failure once and omits the SSH-ready command; normal creation and remote failures are unchanged.
- Adds actual-command tests for human/JSON output using native temporary files and synthetic HTTP responses: two regressions fail before the fix, all six pass after it.
- Verification: all 286 CLI tests, build, Biome and independent focused review pass. Used installed Vitest 2.1.9; strict TypeScript has the same 36 diagnostics as main. No live VM or Pollen used.

gist.headline: Keep the sandbox receipt
gist.blurb: If SSH setup trips after a sandbox is created, the CLI keeps the useful part: its ID. No pretend SSH-ready command, just one clear error and a way to find the sandbox.
gist.summary: The polli CLI prints the created sandbox ID when local SSH setup fails, while retaining exit code 1, reporting the underlying error once, and omitting the SSH-ready command.
gist.impact: Developers can identify a sandbox created before SSH setup failed, without mistaking the partial setup for a successful connection.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a small sandbox garden with a clear ID tag that Polli retrieves after an SSH cable comes loose. A friendly CRT robot shows a single error on its screen; no connected-terminal imagery. Polli wears a tiny tool belt, with lime-green code-plants and warm pastel surroundings.

Cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, with prominent lime green (#ecf874) code-plants, a warm cream background, and dark purple (#110518) outlines.
